findings.title: Squared-budget tolerance changes the identified set under amplitude-unit conversion
findings.description: The numeric 1 in tol=1e-9*max(1,rho^2,J0) has no matching physical unit and dominates small budgets. Exact zero data with rho=1e-6 returns SINGLETON_NUMERIC_BOUNDARY and radius=0 although the proved set is a nonzero full24 ball of radius 3.206791803148725e-7. The retained generic EMPTY and BALL controls also both become radius-zero singletons when Y and rho are scaled by 1e-6. This is a finite wrong output, not an ambiguous ill-conditioned boundary: the generic empty case is below the floor by 75 percent of J0. Negative rho is also accepted although the radius interpretation and rho/ell bounds require rho>=0.
findings.minimal_fix: Use a unit-equivariant squared-amplitude tolerance and explicit nonnegative finite radius domain; separate numerical boundary uncertainty from singleton, with scale and zero-data regressions.

findings.title: Exported coefficient nullspace vectors are still whitened
findings.description: solve_metric creates N=null_space(F/d) at line72 and compact exports its transpose under coefficient_nullspace_directions_2x9. For the nominal common metric, ||F N||_F/||F||_F=0.030178449123981835, so these are not nuisance directions in the declared original moment coordinates and cannot be added to c_M while preserving Fc=a. The correct original directions N/d give 2.5997225981406524e-16. All six common-metric branches exhibit the same issue; raw-I happens to conceal it.
findings.minimal_fix: Export N_c=N_z/d in original coordinates and explicitly name any retained whitened N_z; verify both null equations, M normalization/orthogonality and full24 lifts.
